claims.claim: S1 cannot answer any single user request.
claims.evidence: Two native-prompt author-harness cases contain nonquiet generated speech independently transcribed with sky and blue.

claims.claim: The custom prompt is compatible with the released inference policy.
claims.evidence: Custom-prompt bread and repeat controls produce a startup greeting; native-shaped prompts produce responsive speech on the repeat and factual controls.

claims.claim: Changing history serialization alone fixes the bread failure.
claims.evidence: Raw and canonical history controls both fail to provide a bread answer.

claims.claim: The bread silence is caused by a slow service or input backlog.
claims.evidence: Author-harness bread case recognizes the full question, has no input-clock backlog, and runs below the 480 ms tick budget.

claims.claim: The exact underlying cause of bread-specific silence is known.
claims.evidence: It persists under source simulation parameters, native/task prompts, initial silence, raw/canonical histories and a cache-disabled control. No native THINK control is produced.

limitations: Toy authored synthetic inputs; not a benchmark or evidence of robust S1 instruction following.
The main reference run is one A100 80 GB with all S1 components sharing GPU 0; S2 is absent, so S1/S2 contention cannot cause these results.
Text diagnostic loops are unpaced. Their timing is not a realtime benchmark.
The reference loop retains stock websocket chunk stretching; independent replay retains actual packet arrivals rather than source small-jitter stitching.
Automatic speech transcript is from one contiguous nonquiet response window, preserving its internal gaps; full played PCM remains unchanged.
Independent Whisper input checks confuse synthetic sky/the with similar sounds. They are review-required; S1 itself recovers both complete instructions.
Prompt effects are supported across controls; individual style, language, sampling and cache contributions are not all isolated in the audio run.
Complete-file audio controls produce no ASR or answer. The model is trained for 480 ms packets; these controls do not establish general whole-file capability.
recommendations: Use the native patience/short-clear system prompt and raw assistant history for the S1-only single-question baseline; do not add greeting or wait directives.
Keep the sky question as the current audible S1-only control, with the repeat instruction as a second control.
Do not resume S2 or interruption studies until this baseline is stable; keep bread silence separately marked unresolved.
Use immutable launch-config snapshots and record the exact config loaded by each job.

Present in the author loop too; no input backlog or native THINK. Bread cause unresolved.

failure_mode_synthesis.prevalence: Among four completed main audio controls, two have complete verified speech and two remain quiet. These selected toy controls do not estimate population success rate.
failure_mode_synthesis.root_cause_clustering: Prompt/history/input contracts affect observed policy. Raw history alone does not repair bread. More than one failure mechanism is therefore plausible.
failure_mode_synthesis.design_vs_implementation: Assuming arbitrary prompt prose and whole-file audio would behave like the trained 480 ms interface was a harness design assumption. Requiring S2 metadata for an S1-only run was an implementation defect, now fixed. Bread-specific silence remains an open model/policy question.
failure_mode_synthesis.collective_assessment: Basic S1 speech works on the native baseline. The previous failure cannot be generalized to all single requests; robust task following and bread recipes remain unproven.
